definitions.explanation: A comment or action that indirectly criticizes or mocks someone without naming them directly. The speaker implies criticism through a seemingly general statement that the target (and often the audience) can recognize as aimed at them.

examples.japanese: それは{私|わたし}への{当|あ}てこすりですか。
examples.english: Is that a snide remark directed at me?

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{当|あ}てこすりを{言|い}うのが{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: She's good at making snide remarks.

examples.japanese: {直接|ちょくせつ}{文句|もんく}を{言|い}わずに{当|あ}てこすりばかり{言|い}う{人|ひと}は{信用|しんよう}できない。
examples.english: I can't trust someone who only makes insinuations instead of speaking directly.

notes:
{当|あ}てこすり is derived from the verb {当|あ}てこする (to make a snide remark). The noun form is more commonly used.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {当|あ}てこすりを{言|い}う — to make a snide remark
- {当|あ}てこすりを{言|い}われる — to be the target of insinuation
- ～への{当|あ}てこすり — an insinuation aimed at ~

The key feature of {当|あ}てこすり is its indirectness — the speaker maintains plausible deniability while the intended target understands the criticism. This differs from {皮肉|ひにく} (irony/sarcasm), which may be more openly cutting.
